world.title: Saudi forces intercept missiles after Houthi strikes target ports and refinery
world.summary: Saudi forces said they intercepted missiles and drones targeting Riyadh and other areas on Thursday, as Yemen’s Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition traded attacks on ports and energy infrastructure. The interceptions followed Houthi claims of strikes on Saudi ports and the Ras Tanura refinery, and coalition strikes on
world.content: Saudi forces said they intercepted missiles and drones targeting Riyadh and other areas on Thursday, as Yemen’s Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition traded attacks on ports and energy infrastructure. The interceptions followed Houthi claims of strikes on Saudi ports and the Ras Tanura refinery, and coalition strikes on Hodeidah and other Houthi-held areas in Yemen. Saudi forces said air defenses destroyed two ballistic missiles heading toward Riyadh, a cruise missile in western Saudi Arabia and a drone near Jeddah’s port. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said debris from the intercepted drone caused no civilian injuries. An explosion was heard in Riyadh after authorities issued an aerial-threat alert. The coalition said a projectile hit Jazan port on Wednesday, causing minor damage and no civilian casualties. The Houthis claimed attacks on both Jazan and Jeddah; a strike on Jeddah was not independently confirmed. The Houthis also claimed to have struck Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia’s largest refinery. Satellite images showed thick smoke at the site, and a source familiar with the matter confirmed an attack. The coalition reported intercepting four drones over the area but did not confirm a refinery strike. Saudi authorities and state oil company Aramco did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

world.title: Salvadoran man reaches Spain after judge clears voluntary U.S. departure
world.summary: Kilmar Ábrego García, the Salvadoran man who was mistakenly deported to El Salvador in 2025 and later fought renewed removal efforts, arrived in Madrid on Wednesday after leaving the United States on a commercial flight. His lawyer calls the departure temporary and says he hopes to return to Maryland, where his wife an
world.content: Kilmar Ábrego García, the Salvadoran man who was mistakenly deported to El Salvador in 2025 and later fought renewed removal efforts, arrived in Madrid on Wednesday after leaving the United States on a commercial flight. His lawyer calls the departure temporary and says he hopes to return to Maryland, where his wife and child are U.S. citizens. The Department of Homeland Security says he left under a removal order and will not be allowed back. A federal judge closed Ábrego García’s immigration case after confirming his departure and unsealed an order requiring officials to let him travel without interference. The order required officials to remove his ankle monitor and clear records that could block him from boarding. It allowed him to go to any country willing to accept him. The government did not publicly explain why it had agreed to that arrangement. Ábrego García entered Spain using his Salvadoran passport. His immigration status there remains unclear, and his lawyer said he initially planned a short stay. A separate appeal of the dismissal of U.S. human-smuggling charges is scheduled for February before a three-judge panel of the 6th Circuit Court of Appeals.
world.image_alt: Salvadoran man reaches Spain after judge clears voluntary U.S. departure

world.title: Two charged over alleged theft at Prince William’s country home
world.summary: Two men appeared in court Wednesday charged in connection with a break-in at Anmer Hall, the Norfolk country home of Prince William and Princess Catherine, where prosecutors allege they stole six pairs of cufflinks and a clock. Police arrested the men after investigating reports of suspicious activity at the Sandringha
world.content: Two men appeared in court Wednesday charged in connection with a break-in at Anmer Hall, the Norfolk country home of Prince William and Princess Catherine, where prosecutors allege they stole six pairs of cufflinks and a clock. Police arrested the men after investigating reports of suspicious activity at the Sandringham estate on Monday, Nov. 23; a third suspect remains at large. Prosecutors told Norwich Magistrates’ Court that Mirgen Doku, 34, and Arilen Ndoci, 32, climbed a drainpipe, forced open a window and entered a dressing room. One pair of cufflinks was described in court as “Duke of Edinburgh cufflinks.” The property was unoccupied, and neither man entered a plea at the hearing. The court remanded both men in custody until their next appearance on Monday. Prosecutors also need the attorney general’s permission to proceed with the charge of trespassing on a protected site.
world.image_alt: Two charged over alleged theft at Prince William’s country home

world.title: South African court voids report underpinning Ramaphosa impeachment inquiry
world.summary: South Africa’s Western Cape High Court on Wednesday, Nov. 25, set aside the 2022 parliamentary panel report that underpinned an impeachment inquiry into President Cyril Ramaphosa and voided Parliament’s subsequent steps based on it. The court unanimously ruled that the panel exceeded its mandate and made material error
world.content: South Africa’s Western Cape High Court on Wednesday, Nov. 25, set aside the 2022 parliamentary panel report that underpinned an impeachment inquiry into President Cyril Ramaphosa and voided Parliament’s subsequent steps based on it. The court unanimously ruled that the panel exceeded its mandate and made material errors of law. The ruling removes the inquiry’s current legal foundation, though opposition parties may appeal. The case concerns a February 2020 burglary at Ramaphosa’s Phala Phala farm in Limpopo, where $580,000 was stolen from a sofa. Former spy chief Arthur Fraser alleged that Ramaphosa concealed the theft; the president says the cash came from a legitimate buffalo sale and denies wrongdoing. Prosecutors dropped charges related to Fraser’s complaint in 2024. The judgment addressed the legality of the panel’s report, not whether Ramaphosa committed misconduct. Parliament’s impeachment committee had been due to meet on Nov. 26, and its chair sought legal advice on whether it could proceed. The African Transformation Movement said it was considering an appeal.
world.image_alt: South African court voids report underpinning Ramaphosa impeachment inquiry

world.title: EU leaders open budget talks as €45 billion Ukraine loan divides bloc
world.summary: European Union leaders began a two-day summit in Brussels on Thursday to negotiate the bloc’s 2028-2034 budget and a proposed €45 billion loan to help Ukraine meet its 2027 needs. European Council President António Costa’s revised budget plan is €204 billion below the European Commission’s original proposal; the loan w
world.content: European Union leaders began a two-day summit in Brussels on Thursday to negotiate the bloc’s 2028-2034 budget and a proposed €45 billion loan to help Ukraine meet its 2027 needs. European Council President António Costa’s revised budget plan is €204 billion below the European Commission’s original proposal; the loan would be backed by joint borrowing and split between economic support and military assistance. Ukraine faces an estimated €70 billion funding gap next year, with the loan intended to cover €45 billion and allies outside the EU expected to provide another €25 billion. The budget debate pits governments seeking tighter spending and more money for defence and competitiveness against those defending farming subsidies and funds for poorer regions. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has demanded that all 27 member states share the cost of support for Ukraine, while Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary and Slovakia oppose joining the proposed loan. Merz has warned he could block the broader budget without a collective commitment, drawing criticism from leaders opposed to linking the two issues. Leaders are not expected to settle the budget at this summit; Costa plans further negotiations ahead of the EU’s final leaders’ meeting of the year on Dec. 17-18. Missing the year-end target would not immediately stop EU funding, but member states and the European Parliament must approve the budget legislation in time for spending to begin in January 2028.
world.image_alt: EU leaders open budget talks as €45 billion Ukraine loan divides bloc

world.title: Ukraine says strike on Russian air base damaged five military jets
world.summary: Ukraine’s General Staff said its forces struck Savasleyka air base in Russia’s Nizhny Novgorod region on the night of Nov. 24-25, damaging three MiG-31s and two Su-34s that it said would be unable to fly “for some time.” The base lies about 300 kilometres east of Moscow and hosts aircraft used in Russian missile and gl
world.content: Ukraine’s General Staff said its forces struck Savasleyka air base in Russia’s Nizhny Novgorod region on the night of Nov. 24-25, damaging three MiG-31s and two Su-34s that it said would be unable to fly “for some time.” The base lies about 300 kilometres east of Moscow and hosts aircraft used in Russian missile and glide-bomb attacks. Russia had not commented, and the reported damage had not been independently verified. Kyiv said the strike was part of its campaign against Russian military and energy targets. Ukraine’s own energy system faces renewed Russian attacks. Ukrainian officials also said they struck two refineries in the Samara region; regional governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev said air defences downed more than 145 drones, while local authorities reported one person killed and power outages. Industry sources said Ukrainian drone attacks had reduced Russian refinery processing volumes by 45% since late October. The U.S. State Department separately approved a possible $621.9 million sale of F-16 maintenance support and related equipment to Ukraine; the U.S. government will select a principal contractor through procurement. Ukraine’s General Staff said it was still assessing the damage at the air base and the number of aircraft affected.
world.image_alt: Ukraine says strike on Russian air base damaged five military jets

world.title: Israeli opposition leader Eisenkot seals first pact to replace Netanyahu
world.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, leader of Israel’s Yashar party, has reached a coalition pact with the right-wing opposition party Yisrael Beytenu, the first formal alliance since Israel’s Oct. 27 election. Eisenkot says he aims to form a government by Wednesday, Dec. 2. His mandate expires Dec. 6, though President Isaac Herzog could g
world.content: Gadi Eisenkot, leader of Israel’s Yashar party, has reached a coalition pact with the right-wing opposition party Yisrael Beytenu, the first formal alliance since Israel’s Oct. 27 election. Eisenkot says he aims to form a government by Wednesday, Dec. 2. His mandate expires Dec. 6, though President Isaac Herzog could grant a 14-day extension. Eisenkot’s opposition bloc holds 48 seats in the Knesset, Israel’s 120-seat parliament, while Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc has 53 and Arab-led parties hold 19, leaving no bloc with a majority. The Democrats, led by Yair Golan, have suspended talks after Eisenkot’s outreach to Netanyahu’s Likud party. Eisenkot is also considering support from Arab parties or ultra-Orthodox factions, or a unity government with Likud. If he fails to form a government, Herzog could give another lawmaker a chance, and Israel could hold another election next year.
world.image_alt: Israeli opposition leader Eisenkot seals first pact to replace Netanyahu

world.title: Kim calls for wider tactical nuclear deployment as North Korea expands production
world.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for deploying tactical nuclear weapons across multiple domains and said the country was systematically expanding nuclear-material production, state media reported Thursday. He spoke during a Wednesday inspection of nuclear-material production and weapons research sites, including
world.content: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for deploying tactical nuclear weapons across multiple domains and said the country was systematically expanding nuclear-material production, state media reported Thursday. He spoke during a Wednesday inspection of nuclear-material production and weapons research sites, including a newly built production base and a nuclear-related equipment facility. State media did not identify their locations. Kim said tactical weapons should serve different missions, citing what he described as threats from South Korea and the United States. He again declared North Korea’s nuclear status irreversible and warned that attempts to deny it would be treated as a declaration of war. Pyongyang enshrined its nuclear status in its constitution in 2023. The inspection followed President Donald Trump’s unsuccessful bid to meet Kim during a visit to China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit last week. North Korea did not publicly respond; Trump later said the timing had not been right. South Korea’s defense ministry expressed grave concern over Kim’s stated intention to expand tactical weapons.
world.image_alt: Kim calls for wider tactical nuclear deployment as North Korea expands production

business.title: U.S. inflation hits 3.8%, strengthening case for December Fed hike
business.summary: The U.S. personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge, rose 3.8% year over year in October, while the core measure excluding food and energy reached 3.3%. Both were well above the Fed’s 2% target. Markets were pricing in a quarter-point rate increase at the Fed’s
business.content: The U.S. personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge, rose 3.8% year over year in October, while the core measure excluding food and energy reached 3.3%. Both were well above the Fed’s 2% target. Markets were pricing in a quarter-point rate increase at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting, while investors weighed the possibility of further increases in 2027. The inflation report arrived alongside a revised estimate showing the economy grew at a 4.3% annual rate in the third quarter, with consumer spending and business investment contributing to the expansion. Stocks declined, and inflation-adjusted consumer spending fell in October.
business.image_alt: U.S. inflation hits 3.8%, strengthening case for December Fed hike

business.title: UK discounter Poundland enters administration, putting 11,000 jobs at risk
business.summary: Poundland, the UK’s first and largest nationwide single-price retailer, entered administration on Wednesday after its U.S. owner, Gordon Brothers, failed to agree on a solvent sale, putting about 11,000 jobs and roughly 600 stores in the UK and Ireland at risk. AlixPartners, the restructuring consultancy appointed as a
business.content: Poundland, the UK’s first and largest nationwide single-price retailer, entered administration on Wednesday after its U.S. owner, Gordon Brothers, failed to agree on a solvent sale, putting about 11,000 jobs and roughly 600 stores in the UK and Ireland at risk. AlixPartners, the restructuring consultancy appointed as administrator, said stores and distribution centres would continue operating while it pursued a sale of the company or its assets, in whole or in parts. The collapse followed worsening access to working capital before Christmas, which Poundland managing director Barry Williams said had left the business unable to operate as a going concern. Gordon Brothers disputed claims that it had cut off funding and said it had released cash when requested. Gordon Brothers said it had provided £85 million in financing and backed £100 million in cost savings, but maintained that Poundland remained vulnerable to inflation and weaker sales or margins. The UK Parliament’s Business and Trade Committee has recalled Gordon Brothers’ regional managing director, Mark Newton-Jones, for public questioning as administrators continue seeking buyers.
business.image_alt: UK discounter Poundland enters administration, putting 11,000 jobs at risk

business.title: Vance says Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces no probe, needs no pardon
business.summary: Vice President JD Vance said Wednesday that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was not under investigation and did not need a pardon, contradicting President Donald Trump’s earlier claim that an investigation had exonerated Huang. The Justice Department had not formally investigated Huang before Trump urged Nvidia’s board to rest
business.content: Vice President JD Vance said Wednesday that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was not under investigation and did not need a pardon, contradicting President Donald Trump’s earlier claim that an investigation had exonerated Huang. The Justice Department had not formally investigated Huang before Trump urged Nvidia’s board to restore him as chief executive; Attorney General Todd Blanche based his assessment on investigations into two Nvidia customers, Reuters reported. Huang resigned on Nov. 12 after reports of extramarital affairs emerged. He acknowledged infidelities and faced allegations involving a woman suspected of links to Chinese intelligence. The board reinstated him Monday. Lawmakers have questioned how the administration assessed national-security risks and influenced the board’s decision. Huang is scheduled for a closed-door congressional interview on Dec. 1 and a public Senate Banking Committee hearing on Dec. 3.
business.image_alt: Vance says Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces no probe, needs no pardon

business.title: Anthropic shares fall below $83 IPO price
business.summary: Shares of Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI assistant, traded around $80.50 on Nov. 25, below its $83 initial public offering price and nearly 30% below its $111.50 opening price on Nov. 19. Among 86 Nasdaq-100 companies with positive earnings multiples and available forecast data, 60 had higher earnings estima
business.content: Shares of Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI assistant, traded around $80.50 on Nov. 25, below its $83 initial public offering price and nearly 30% below its $111.50 opening price on Nov. 19. Among 86 Nasdaq-100 companies with positive earnings multiples and available forecast data, 60 had higher earnings estimates over the past three months, but 37 of those stocks still fell. CNBC reported that a weak public-market reception could complicate OpenAI’s planned 2027 IPO and reduce the value of shares Anthropic might sell to finance future operations. Anthropic had more than $200 billion in cash after its IPO, but its prospectus listed over $900 billion in future financial commitments.
business.image_alt: Anthropic shares fall below $83 IPO price

business.title: SpaceX and Musk pledge shares to active Trump Accounts
business.summary: SpaceX said on Wednesday, Nov. 25, that it will give one newly issued Class A share to every currently active Trump Account, a tax-advantaged investment account for U.S. children. Chief Executive Elon Musk pledged to match the company’s gift. The pledge would mean two SpaceX shares per active account, but the number of
business.content: SpaceX said on Wednesday, Nov. 25, that it will give one newly issued Class A share to every currently active Trump Account, a tax-advantaged investment account for U.S. children. Chief Executive Elon Musk pledged to match the company’s gift. The pledge would mean two SpaceX shares per active account, but the number of active accounts is unclear: the White House said nearly 70 million had been created by October. At Wednesday’s closing price of $127.44, gifts to 70 million accounts would total about $17.8 billion in shares, though that calculation assumes every account is active and the price holds. Eligible children born from 2025 through 2028 can receive a one-time $1,000 federal contribution. Friends and family have deposited more than $1 billion, while total deposits, including federal and philanthropic contributions, exceed $9 billion, according to Treasury figures reported by Fox Business. SpaceX said it would transfer its shares next month; Musk said his personal shares would follow when his lockup expires in June 2027.
business.image_alt: SpaceX and Musk pledge shares to active Trump Accounts

business.title: S&P puts Nvidia credit rating on downgrade watch over governance
business.summary: S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia’s AA credit rating on negative watch Wednesday, saying it could cut the chipmaker’s rating by one notch within 90 days because of rising management and governance risks. The agency said the departure and reinstatement of Chief Executive Jensen Huang left questions about board oversight,
business.content: S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia’s AA credit rating on negative watch Wednesday, saying it could cut the chipmaker’s rating by one notch within 90 days because of rising management and governance risks. The agency said the departure and reinstatement of Chief Executive Jensen Huang left questions about board oversight, independence and succession planning unresolved. It said it had not identified any remedial action by the board and plans to meet with directors and management. A one-notch cut to AA- would leave Nvidia’s rating at investment grade but could raise borrowing costs. Moody’s kept its Aa1 rating and stable outlook, saying Huang’s return reduced near-term uncertainty over business execution while governance and regulatory questions remained. S&P expects to conclude its review within 90 days.
business.image_alt: S&P puts Nvidia credit rating on downgrade watch over governance

business.title: South Korea raises key rate to 3.25% as AI exports lift outlook
business.summary: South Korea’s central bank raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter of a percentage point to 3.25% on Thursday, its third increase since July and the highest level in two years, as inflation remained above target and strong semiconductor exports prompted higher growth forecasts. The Bank of Korea lifted its 2026
business.content: South Korea’s central bank raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter of a percentage point to 3.25% on Thursday, its third increase since July and the highest level in two years, as inflation remained above target and strong semiconductor exports prompted higher growth forecasts. The Bank of Korea lifted its 2026 growth estimate to 3.9% from 3.3% and its 2027 forecast to 4.1% from 2.9%, citing robust demand for AI-related chips. Consumer prices rose 2.8% in October, compared with the central bank’s 2% target. The bank said higher energy costs and strengthening demand could keep inflation above target for a considerable time. It also warned that rising property prices and household borrowing pose risks to financial stability, while consumer spending remains constrained by prices, stagnant wages and debt payments. The decision followed rate increases in July and August and a pause in October. Five of seven policy-board members backed the move, while two favored holding rates at 3%; the bank’s next scheduled meeting is Jan. 14.
business.image_alt: South Korea raises key rate to 3.25% as AI exports lift outlook

business.title: AI shares slide again as Nvidia rebound fails to revive investor confidence
business.summary: U.S. technology stocks fell Wednesday, with the Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500 each closing down less than 1% after steeper early losses. Nvidia fell as much as 9% during trading. The retreat followed Nvidia’s board reinstating co-founder Jensen Huang as chief executive. Huang had resigned on Nov. 12 amid scrutiny of his condu
business.content: U.S. technology stocks fell Wednesday, with the Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500 each closing down less than 1% after steeper early losses. Nvidia fell as much as 9% during trading. The retreat followed Nvidia’s board reinstating co-founder Jensen Huang as chief executive. Huang had resigned on Nov. 12 amid scrutiny of his conduct and national-security concerns; investors remain uneasy about AI spending and the chipmaker’s China business. Investors are questioning whether the vast buildout of AI data centers will generate returns that justify its cost. Financing links among chipmakers, cloud providers and AI developers can also make it difficult to distinguish demand from purchases supported by suppliers’ own funding. Some business customers are now asking whether AI investments improve productivity, cut costs or add revenue, rather than treating adoption itself as a measure of success. Nvidia’s internal review and government inquiries remain active, and Huang is scheduled to testify before the U.S. Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3 about chip-export controls. Republican leaders of three House panels also said Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter remained scheduled for congressional interviews in early December.
business.image_alt: AI shares slide again as Nvidia rebound fails to revive investor confidence

science.title: November Beaver supermoon brightens skies worldwide; next expected in December
science.summary: The November full moon, known as the Beaver Moon, reached fullness on Nov. 24 and appeared as a supermoon because it coincided with the Moon’s passage near its closest point to Earth. NASA says a full supermoon can appear up to 14% larger and 30% brighter than a full moon near the farthest point in its orbit, although
science.content: The November full moon, known as the Beaver Moon, reached fullness on Nov. 24 and appeared as a supermoon because it coincided with the Moon’s passage near its closest point to Earth. NASA says a full supermoon can appear up to 14% larger and 30% brighter than a full moon near the farthest point in its orbit, although the size difference can be hard to detect with the naked eye. Photographers captured the event over city skylines and landmarks around the world. The Nov. 24 display was the first of three consecutive supermoons spanning late 2026 and early 2027, with the next expected on Dec. 24 and another on Jan. 22, 2027. The December event is expected to be the final supermoon of 2026 and the year’s largest full moon.
science.image_alt: November Beaver supermoon brightens skies worldwide; next expected in December

science.title: Four Guangxi fossil teeth point to Denisovans and another ancient lineage
science.summary: Researchers analyzing four fossil teeth from two caves in China’s Guangxi region identified Denisovan-related remains and evidence of a potentially distinct ancient human lineage, according to a study published in Nature on Nov. 25. The two Longchuandong teeth align with Denisovans, while two teeth from Chuanshandong—a
science.content: Researchers analyzing four fossil teeth from two caves in China’s Guangxi region identified Denisovan-related remains and evidence of a potentially distinct ancient human lineage, according to a study published in Nature on Nov. 25. The two Longchuandong teeth align with Denisovans, while two teeth from Chuanshandong—at least 100,800 years old—have traits that do not readily match any known East Asian Homo group. The findings suggest different archaic human populations lived in southern China during overlapping periods, but researchers cannot yet confidently assign the Chuanshandong teeth to a named group. Warm, humid conditions in the region hinder ancient DNA preservation, so researchers analyzed tooth shape and proteins. They say more fossils and molecular evidence are needed to establish the teeth’s evolutionary relationships.
science.image_alt: Four Guangxi fossil teeth point to Denisovans and another ancient lineage

science.title: Neolithic tomb pots point to fermented milk offerings in Denmark
science.summary: Researchers studying 330 Neolithic pots from western Zealand, Denmark, found corrosion on 31; 29 came from passage tombs. In experiments with reconstructed vessels, fresh, unpasteurized milk produced damage resembling the marks on ancient pottery, while beer and mead did not. The findings, published in Antiquity, sugge
science.content: Researchers studying 330 Neolithic pots from western Zealand, Denmark, found corrosion on 31; 29 came from passage tombs. In experiments with reconstructed vessels, fresh, unpasteurized milk produced damage resembling the marks on ancient pottery, while beer and mead did not. The findings, published in Antiquity, suggest fermented dairy may have been placed with the dead, although corrosion alone cannot identify the contents with certainty. The results challenge an earlier interpretation that the corroded pots held beer, an idea based partly on evidence from brewing communities elsewhere. Fermentation makes milk more acidic, and the researchers say fermented dairy products could also have been easier to digest and lasted longer. Lead author Lone Claudi-Hansen, an archaeologist, said she hopes to examine pottery from other parts of Denmark to see whether the same pattern appears elsewhere.
science.image_alt: Neolithic tomb pots point to fermented milk offerings in Denmark

science.title: Stanford researchers find nanoscale niobium phosphide wires outperform copper
science.summary: Stanford University researchers reported that ultrathin niobium phosphide ribbons conduct electricity more efficiently than copper wires of comparable size, with resistivity falling as the ribbons narrow. The study, published in Nature, tested ribbons as small as 5–6 nanometers wide and about 1.5 nanometers thick. Resi
science.content: Stanford University researchers reported that ultrathin niobium phosphide ribbons conduct electricity more efficiently than copper wires of comparable size, with resistivity falling as the ribbons narrow. The study, published in Nature, tested ribbons as small as 5–6 nanometers wide and about 1.5 nanometers thick. Resistance in the tiny connections linking transistors can delay signals in advanced chips. Researchers disagree about whether the material’s topological properties explain the drop in resistivity. Outside scientists questioned whether a niobium surface layer influenced the measurements, and Stanford physicist and study leader Eric Pop acknowledged that other explanations remain possible.
science.image_alt: Stanford researchers find nanoscale niobium phosphide wires outperform copper

science.title: Euclid finds most distant confirmed quasar, with 360-million-solar-mass black hole
science.summary: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has identified the most distant confirmed quasar yet, J1504+6252, nicknamed Dún Aonghasa, seen as it was about 630 million years after the Big Bang. Its central black hole has an estimated mass of 360 million suns. The discovery pushes the quasar record about 40 millio
science.content: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has identified the most distant confirmed quasar yet, J1504+6252, nicknamed Dún Aonghasa, seen as it was about 630 million years after the Big Bang. Its central black hole has an estimated mass of 360 million suns. The discovery pushes the quasar record about 40 million years earlier than the previous one. The black hole’s mass is difficult to explain because observations indicate it is feeding relatively slowly. Researchers say it must have grown faster earlier or formed from an unusually massive initial “seed.” Euclid identified the candidate in its survey; follow-up observations from the Keck Observatory, Hubble, the Large Binocular Telescope and the James Webb Space Telescope confirmed and characterized it. The study appeared Nov. 24 in Astronomy & Astrophysics. Additional Euclid and Webb observations will test whether other early quasars show the same pattern.
science.image_alt: Euclid finds most distant confirmed quasar, with 360-million-solar-mass black hole

science.title: California king tides break coastal records, partially collapse Pacifica pier
science.summary: California’s king tides and powerful surf flooded coastal communities on Nov. 25, set water-level records at several monitoring stations and tore apart part of Pacifica’s municipal pier. San Diego, Los Angeles and Monterey reached their highest recorded coastal water levels; waves at San Francisco’s Ocean Beach reached
science.content: California’s king tides and powerful surf flooded coastal communities on Nov. 25, set water-level records at several monitoring stations and tore apart part of Pacifica’s municipal pier. San Diego, Los Angeles and Monterey reached their highest recorded coastal water levels; waves at San Francisco’s Ocean Beach reached a reported 9.14 metres. The highest tides of the year, produced by the alignment of the moon and sun, coincided with unusually warm Pacific waters linked to a strong El Niño. Human-caused sea-level rise also contributed to elevated water levels. Coastal waters along much of California were more than 5°C above average, further raising local sea levels. The peak astronomical tides are easing, but forecasters expect more king tides in December and January. A Pacific storm could bring heavy rain, strong southerly winds and storm surge to central California around Dec. 1. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie said the city expects further high tides.
science.image_alt: California king tides break coastal records, partially collapse Pacifica pier

science.title: Super El Niño nears record strength as winter risks spread worldwide
science.summary: The World Meteorological Organization says the El Niño warming the central and eastern tropical Pacific is expected to intensify and peak in December, with sea-surface temperatures in the Niño 3.4 region forecast to reach about 3.7°C above normal in October-December. The agency puts the chance of the event lasting thro
science.content: The World Meteorological Organization says the El Niño warming the central and eastern tropical Pacific is expected to intensify and peak in December, with sea-surface temperatures in the Niño 3.4 region forecast to reach about 3.7°C above normal in October-December. The agency puts the chance of the event lasting through February 2027 at nearly 100%; U.S. forecasters estimate a 60% chance it will be the strongest since records began in 1950. Forecasts point to warmer conditions across much of northern North America and wetter weather in parts of the southern United States, though a disrupted polar vortex could still bring brief spells of Arctic cold to Canada. California has already faced coastal flooding during unusually high tides and large Pacific swells. Researchers say this unusually strong event will test forecast models that have limited experience with extreme El Niños. The U.S. Climate Prediction Center expects strong conditions to persist into early 2027.
science.image_alt: Super El Niño nears record strength as winter risks spread worldwide

science.title: FCC approves SpaceX AI satellite plan as astronomers warn of debris
science.summary: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission approved SpaceX’s plan for up to one million Starmind computing satellites, while astronomers and space researchers warned that a constellation of that scale could increase collision risks, threaten observations of the night sky and add pollution when satellites re-enter the a
science.content: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission approved SpaceX’s plan for up to one million Starmind computing satellites, while astronomers and space researchers warned that a constellation of that scale could increase collision risks, threaten observations of the night sky and add pollution when satellites re-enter the atmosphere. This is the first authorization for a full constellation of orbital AI data centers, but the FCC deferred a decision on how to dispose of satellites above 600 kilometers, saying SpaceX had not provided enough information about its plans. Associate Professor Michael Brown, an astronomer at Monash University, said a five-year satellite lifespan would mean more than 500 launches or re-entries a day at full scale. He warned that frequent re-entries could affect the upper atmosphere and ozone layer. The FCC’s approval focused on radio-frequency use; experts said it did not assess effects on optical astronomy or emissions from launches.
science.image_alt: FCC approves SpaceX AI satellite plan as astronomers warn of debris

sports.content: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy missed practice Wednesday with an ankle injury, leaving his status uncertain for Sunday's NFC West game against Seattle. Coach Kyle Shanahan said the injury is not a high-ankle sprain and described Purdy as day to day. Purdy hurt his ankle in the second quarter of the 49ers' 35-10 win over the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City on Sunday but stayed in the game. Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold, who missed two games with quadriceps and rib injuries, practiced fully Wednesday. Coach Mike Macdonald said the plan is for him to start if practice goes well. San Francisco (9-1) hosts Seattle (6-4) at Levi's Stadium, with the Seahawks three games behind the 49ers in the NFC West. San Francisco won the teams' first meeting 32-29 in Seattle on Oct. 11. The teams will provide further practice updates before Friday's official injury designations.

sports.title: Manchester United rally but concede late equaliser at Sporting
sports.summary: Manchester United came from behind to lead before conceding a late equaliser in a 2-2 draw with Sporting CP in Lisbon on November 25. United captain Bruno Fernandes scored twice against his former club, but a late goalkeeping error cost new head coach Mauricio Pochettino his first win. Sporting striker Luis Suárez scor
sports.content: Manchester United came from behind to lead before conceding a late equaliser in a 2-2 draw with Sporting CP in Lisbon on November 25. United captain Bruno Fernandes scored twice against his former club, but a late goalkeeping error cost new head coach Mauricio Pochettino his first win. Sporting striker Luis Suárez scored from the penalty spot and later levelled after United goalkeeper Senne Lammens spilled a routine ball into his path. The draw followed a 4-0 loss to Liverpool in Pochettino’s first match. United entered the Sporting game 19th in the Premier League with eight points from 11 matches. Fernandes described the team’s league position as “fragile” and called on his teammates to fight together. Fernandes played for Sporting before joining United in January 2020, and the Portuguese club honoured him before kick-off. He has put contract discussions on hold until United start winning. His current deal expires in June 2027, with the club holding an option to extend it. United’s next match is at home to Brentford on Saturday, November 28.

sports.title: MLB teams rush to sign stars before December 1 labor deadline
sports.summary: The New York Mets agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with two-time American League Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal, the largest guaranteed contract ever for a pitcher, during Major League Baseball’s 2026-27 offseason. The Chicago Cubs agreed to five-year, $120 million deals with starter Trevor Rogers and J
sports.content: The New York Mets agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with two-time American League Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal, the largest guaranteed contract ever for a pitcher, during Major League Baseball’s 2026-27 offseason. The Chicago Cubs agreed to five-year, $120 million deals with starter Trevor Rogers and Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato. The Baltimore Orioles signed right-hander Freddy Peralta for five years and $125 million, while the Toronto Blue Jays agreed to a five-year, $80 million deal with Japanese pitcher Kaima Taira. The Colorado Rockies added starters David Peterson and Patrick Sandoval, and the Detroit Tigers signed veteran Kevin Gausman to a one-year, $25 million contract. Teams are racing to complete transactions before Major League Baseball’s collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on December 1. A lockout is expected to halt signings and trades until a new agreement allows activity to resume. Several top free agents remain unsigned, including outfielders Seiya Suzuki and Randy Arozarena, while the Cubs continue to seek rotation help. Whether teams can resume roster moves after December 1 depends on labor negotiations.

Khawaja’s draft says the squad knew the ball was being altered in South Africa, without specif
sports.content: Former Australia batter Usman Khawaja has proposed a joint statement accepting team-wide responsibility for the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, saying Australia captain Pat Cummins’s criticism of his account hurt him personally. Khawaja’s draft says the squad knew the ball was being altered in South Africa, without specifying sandpaper, and acknowledges the penalties imposed on Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft. Khawaja says he did not want Cummins removed as captain. Greenberg told Khawaja he was unsure whether the proposal would “fly.” Cricket Australia plans an independent forum for players and staff to share their recollections but will not reopen its investigation or impose new sanctions. It has backed Cummins to remain captain. Khawaja, Warner and Bancroft say knowledge extended beyond the three players punished, while Cummins and fellow bowlers deny knowing sandpaper would be used.

sports.title: Raheem Sterling receives suspended sentence and two-year driving ban
sports.summary: Former England forward Raheem Sterling received a 12-month prison sentence, suspended for 18 months, after admitting dangerous driving while using nitrous oxide before crashing his Lamborghini in Hampshire on May 28. Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court also banned the 31-year-old from driving for two years and ordered him t
sports.content: Former England forward Raheem Sterling received a 12-month prison sentence, suspended for 18 months, after admitting dangerous driving while using nitrous oxide before crashing his Lamborghini in Hampshire on May 28. Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court also banned the 31-year-old from driving for two years and ordered him to complete 100 hours of unpaid work. He must retake a driving test before regaining a licence. Sterling pleaded guilty in September to dangerous driving, possessing six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen. The court heard he drove on the M25, M3, A327 and Minley Road before his car struck a roadside barrier or gate. No other vehicle was involved and no one was injured. District Judge Kirsty Allman said she took into account his guilty plea, previously clean record, charitable work and voluntary use of addiction services when sentencing him. Sterling, who scored 20 goals in 82 England appearances, is without a club after leaving Feyenoord.

sports.content: London Broncos will return to rugby league’s Super League in 2027 as its 15th club after the competition approved expansion from 14 teams. The London side earned the place after winning the Championship League Leaders’ Shield, Grand Final and 1895 Cup in 2026, although its 16th-place finish in the IMG club gradings did not qualify it for automatic promotion. Barrow Raiders, initially considered for the place, and the Rugby Football League concluded that Barrow would not be ready for top-flight competition next season. London’s inclusion was also a prerequisite in ongoing investment talks involving Australia’s National Rugby League, the Guardian reported. The 2027 season begins on January 28, and the full fixture list is due on December 3.

sports.title: Corum rushes for 184 yards as Rams beat Packers 26-13
sports.summary: The Los Angeles Rams beat the Green Bay Packers 26-13 at SoFi Stadium on Wednesday, Nov. 25, extending their winning streak to five and improving to 7-4 in the National Football Conference (NFC) playoff race. Rams running back Blake Corum rushed for a career-high 184 yards and a touchdown on his 26th birthday, while ru
sports.content: The Los Angeles Rams beat the Green Bay Packers 26-13 at SoFi Stadium on Wednesday, Nov. 25, extending their winning streak to five and improving to 7-4 in the National Football Conference (NFC) playoff race. Rams running back Blake Corum rushed for a career-high 184 yards and a touchdown on his 26th birthday, while running back Kyren Williams also scored. The teams were tied 13-13 at halftime, but Los Angeles shut out Green Bay after the break. Packers quarterback Jordan Love threw two interceptions, and the Rams controlled the ball for 23 minutes and 45 seconds of the second half. Los Angeles leaned on the run with leading receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams sidelined by injuries. Packers wide receiver Christian Watson left with a concussion after a second-quarter hit by Rams safety Kamren Kinchens, who was ejected after video review. Watson had four catches for 65 yards and a touchdown before the injury. The Rams next host the Kansas City Chiefs on Dec. 3; Green Bay visits the New Orleans Saints on Dec. 6.

sports.summary: The NFL’s Thanksgiving week schedule now spans Wednesday through Friday. It opened with the league’s first Thanksgiving Eve game, with the Green Bay Packers visiting the Los Angeles Rams, followed by three Thanksgiving Day games and a Black Friday matchup. Netflix, CBS, Fox, NBC and Prime Video are carrying the games n
sports.content: The NFL’s Thanksgiving week schedule now spans Wednesday through Friday. It opened with the league’s first Thanksgiving Eve game, with the Green Bay Packers visiting the Los Angeles Rams, followed by three Thanksgiving Day games and a Black Friday matchup. Netflix, CBS, Fox, NBC and Prime Video are carrying the games nationally. Thursday’s opener pairs the 8-2 Chicago Bears and 8-2 Detroit Lions; the winner takes sole possession of first place in the NFC North. The 3-7 Philadelphia Eagles then face the 5-6 Dallas Cowboys, before the 8-2 Kansas City Chiefs visit the 9-1 Buffalo Bills in a matchup with implications for the AFC’s top seed. On Friday, the 8-2 Denver Broncos visit the 6-4 Pittsburgh Steelers, who have lost two straight and are turning to Mason Rudolph at quarterback. Chicago and Detroit are tied atop the NFC North, while Buffalo holds the AFC’s No. 1 seed.
